# ✋ Real-Time Hand Tracking

A real-time hand tracking project built with** ** **Python** ,** ** **OpenCV** , and** ** **MediaPipe** .

The project uses a webcam to detect human hands and track their** ****21 hand landmarks** in real time. The detected landmarks are projected onto the camera frame, allowing the hand structure to be visualized and used as the basis for further computer vision and 3D projects.

***Readme generated by AI.***

---

## ✨ Features

* 🎥 Real-time webcam input
* ✋ Hand detection using MediaPipe
* 🖐️ Support for tracking up to two hands
* 📍 Detection of 21 landmarks for each hand
* 🎯 Conversion of normalized landmark coordinates into image pixel coordinates
* 🟢 Real-time visualization of hand landmarks
* 📏 Custom connections between selected landmarks
* 🔄 Real-time processing of consecutive video frames

---

## 🧠 How It Works

The application follows this pipeline:

```text
Webcam
   │
   ▼
OpenCV
   │
   ▼
Video Frame
   │
   ▼
BGR → RGB Conversion
   │
   ▼
MediaPipe Image
   │
   ▼
Hand Landmarker
   │
   ▼
21 Hand Landmarks
   │
   ▼
Pixel Coordinates
   │
   ▼
Visualization
```

Each detected hand is represented by** ** **21 landmarks** , each containing:

* `x` → horizontal position
* `y` → vertical position
* `z` → relative depth

The** **`x` and** **`y` coordinates provided by MediaPipe are normalized between** **`0` and** **`1`. They are converted into pixel coordinates based on the dimensions of the camera frame before being drawn with OpenCV.

---

## 📍 Hand Landmarks

MediaPipe assigns a fixed index to each landmark:

|  Index | Landmark      |
| -----: | ------------- |
|      0 | Wrist         |
|   1–4 | Thumb         |
|   5–8 | Index Finger  |
|  9–12 | Middle Finger |
| 13–16 | Ring Finger   |
| 17–20 | Pinky         |

For example:

```python
hand[4]
```

represents the** ** **tip of the thumb** , while:

```python
hand[8]
```

represents the** ** **tip of the index finger** .

These fixed landmark indices make it possible to create custom geometric structures and interactions based on the position of specific parts of the hand.

## 📦 Installation

Clone the repository:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/YOUR_REPOSITORY.git
```

Enter the project directory:

```bash
cd YOUR_REPOSITORY
```

Install the required dependencies:

```bash
pip install opencv-python mediapipe numpy
```

---

## 🤖 MediaPipe Model

The project uses the** ****MediaPipe Hand Landmarker** model.

Download the required** **`.task` model file and place it in the project directory.

The expected structure is:

```text
project/
│
├── main.py
├── hand_landmarker.task
└── README.md
```

Make sure that the path used in the Python code matches the location of the model file.

---

## ▶️ Run the Project

Start the application with:

```bash
python main.py
```

Make sure your webcam is connected and accessible by OpenCV.

Once the program starts, place your hands in front of the camera to see the detected landmarks in real time.

---

## 📐 Current Landmark Connections

The project currently allows custom connections between specific landmarks.

For example, the tips of the thumb and index finger can be connected:

```text
Thumb ───────── Index
```

When two hands are detected, corresponding landmarks can also be connected:

```text
Left Thumb  ───────── Right Thumb

Left Index  ───────── Right Index
```

This creates a geometric structure between the tracked points.

## 🎯 Project Goal

The long-term goal of this project is to explore how real-time hand tracking can be used to extract** ****2D and 3D spatial information** from human hands and transform that information into interactive geometric structures.

The project started as an experiment with hand landmark detection and is evolving toward a more advanced system for** ** **3D spatial tracking and computer vision** .
